title: Origin of the state
summary: Between 4100 and about 3000 BCE, Uruk in southern Mesopotamia was the largest urban centre and the hub of trade and administration. Uruk is also known for the rise of writing about 3200 BCE and the invention of the cylinder seal. Administrative devices such as cylinder seals and numerical tablets date to the Late Uruk period, about 3350 to 3100 BCE.

uncertainty.note: Late Uruk period state institutions, cylinder seals, and proto-cuneiform bureaucratic texts date from ca. 3350 to 3100 BCE.

as_recorded.value: Between 4100 & circa 3000 BCE, Uruk was the largest urban center & the hub of trade & administration.

where.historical_name: Uruk (Unug), southern Mesopotamia, the earliest primary state and urban metropolis

importance.justification: The emergence of institutionalized state governance, social stratification, and bureaucratic monopoly on legitimate authority transformed human organization from kinship bands into centralized societies.
